result.target_summary: On July 24, 2024, the Board authorized a $25 billion common stock repurchase program effective August 1, 2024, replacing the previous program authorized in 2021, modified in 2023, and expired on August 1, 2024.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures cover the Board's authorization of a $25 billion common stock repurchase program. 2023 describes the authorization in Oct 2021 and modifications in Sept 2023. 2024 describes the new authorization in July 2024 replacing the previous one. They share the specific topic of the authorized repurchase program.

The 2023 disclosure (bac_2023_7_D166) includes details on actual repurchases made during the year ($4.6 billion) and remaining authority. The 2024 disclosure (bac_2024_7_D175) reports actual repurchases made during 2024 ($13.1 billion). Both relate to the execution of repurchase programs authorized by the Board.

comparisons.peer_topic: Shareholder Returns and Capital Repurchase Program
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi returned $6.7 billion to shareholders in 2024 via dividends and repurchases, and authorized a new $20 billion multiyear repurchase program in January 2025 with $1.5 billion planned for Q1 2025, subject to regulatory capital uncertainty.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C disclose recent Board authorizations of new common stock repurchase programs with specific dollar amounts and effective dates, though the timing and regulatory context differ. BAC authorized a $25 billion program effective August 1, 2024, replacing an expired program. Citi authorized a new $20 billion multiyear program in January 2025, with $1.5 billion planned for Q1 2025, explicitly subject to uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements. While both represent new capital return authorizations, Citi's program is contingent on future regulatory assessment, whereas BAC's was a replacement of a completed prior authorization.

sentences.text: On July 24, 2024, the Board authorized a $25 billion common stock repurchase program, effective August 1, 2024, which replaced the Corporation's previous program that was initially authorized by the Board in 2021, modified in 2023 and expired on August 1, 2024.

• Citi returned $6.7 billion to common shareholders in the form of dividends ($4.2 billion) and share repurchases ($2.5 billion) in 2024. As previously disclosed, on January 13, 2025, Citigroup's Board of Directors authorized a new, multiyear $20 billion common stock repurchase program, with planned repurchases of $1.5 billion during the first quarter of 2025, subject to market conditions and other factors. After the first quarter of 2025, Citi will continue to assess the level of common share repurchases on a quarter-by-quarter basis given uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements, among other factors.
